inside an X.509 GeneralName. X.400 addresses were parsed as an ASN1_STRING but
the public structure definition for GENERAL_NAME incorrectly specified the type
of the x400Address field as ASN1_TYPE. This field is subsequently interpreted by
the OpenSSL function GENERAL_NAME_cmp as an ASN1_TYPE rather than an

provide both the certificate chain and CRL, neither of which need to have a
valid signature. If the attacker only controls one of these inputs, the other

CVE-2026-105483.description:
A flaw in Node.js TLS hostname verification allows a certificate without a matching IP address SAN to authenticate a connection to an IPv4 address when the host is written with non-ASCII characters, such as fullwidth digits (`１２７.0.0.1`).

`tls.checkServerIdentity()` did not recognize such hosts as IP addresses, even though they normalize and resolve to a regular IPv4 address, and matched them against the certificate DNS names and Common Name instead. A certificate containing `DNS:127.0.0.1` or `DNS:*.0.0.1` could therefore be accepted for an IP endpoint it was not issued for. This is a regression introduced after the fix for CVE-2026-48618.

This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x** and **24.x**.

CVE-2026-62337.description: SNARK Verifier is a generic (S)NARK verifier. Prior to 0.2.5, the Halo 2 aggregation circuit can mishandle proof points encoded as the point at infinity. `EcPointLoader::multi_scalar_multiplication` places a `Value::Assigned(_)` base paired with `Value::Constant(ONE)` into its unscaled variable-base list and passes it directly to `sum_with_const`. CVE-2026-99623.title: drm/amdgpu: Clamp the ATIF backlight curve to its 99 points
CVE-2026-99623.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: Clamp the ATIF backlight curve to its 99 points

amdgpu_atif_query_backlight_caps() stores the firmware's number_of_points
as data_points but copies only the 99 points that luminance_data[] holds.
number_of_points is a u8, so a firmware table that claims more makes the
custom curve code in amdgpu_dm index past the array, and
dm_query_extended_brightness_caps() copy past the end of the
data_points[] buffer it fills

Clamp the count to ATIF_QBTC_MAX_DATA_POINTS and warn, since a table
that claims more is a firmware bug

CVE-2026-99656.title: mm/madvise: fix data loss from MADV_FREE on a KSM page
CVE-2026-99656.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/madvise: fix data loss from MADV_FREE on a KSM page

MADV_FREE can clear the dirty flag of a singly mapped KSM folio. The
folio remains in the stable tree and can gain new mappings without being
dirtied again. Once marked lazyfree, reclaim can discard data that those
mappings still need.

KSM always marks a folio dirty when converting it to a KSM folio in
try_to_merge_one_page(). Marking a folio lazyfree clears PG_swapbacked
but leaves PG_dirty unchanged. Preserving PG_dirty makes reclaim restore
PG_swapbacked instead of discarding the folio. This also protects folios
that were already lazyfree when KSM converted them.

Skip KSM folios before clearing their dirty flag, checking under the
folio lock to serialize with KSM conversion.
